gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words read as solid blocks, with bowls left open on one side. Nippo is the one with the wire-cut lines and the technical edge, while the body font does the quiet work of keeping text steady.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable and sturdy, Noto Sans Lepcha has curves that stay wide open and a lowercase built like cast iron capitals. Nippo draws attention; this one holds it.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Nippo stands its small letters nearly as tall as capitals, drawn with no thinning anywhere along the stroke. And Noto Sans Limbu follows with tall-bodied lowercase and gaping curves, so the two read as one family of upright shapes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Nippo traces every letter as if with one marker tip. Noto Sans Lydian sits beneath it with capitals barely taller than lowercase and a spring-wide opening, so the heading's wiry line and the body's relaxed shapes share the page comfortably.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Noto Sans Mahajani stands its lowercase tall against the capitals, with a funnel-wide throat in the e. Over a longer passage that height makes lines feel brisk, and Noto Sans Mahajani never tangles the way Nippo's bent-paperclip strokes might.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Noto Sans Malayalam lets the middle zone dominate each line. Nippo, drawn like a single thick thread, makes the headline, and the body's generous s curves keep the text beneath it easy to follow.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Lowercase rising close to capitals, with curvy letters that feel unclamped, gives this sans-serif its relaxed look. Noto Sans Mandaic works well at a modest size, leaving Nippo's string-steady strokes to take the larger sizes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Clean and neutral, Noto Sans Marchen ends its curves in clear daylight while sharing Nippo's tall small letters. But Nippo draws its plain constant-width lines like wire, so it stands out where the body simply recedes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Noto Sans Medefaidrin lifts its lowercase high and keeps ink from pooling where curves turn in. Noto Sans Medefaidrin would read as a smooth, modern stretch of text beside Nippo's wiry, evenly weighted display letters.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui reads with daylight through every curve and a lowercase standing tall against its capitals. Nippo is best at flat, wire-like display lines, while this body keeps text open.
